title: When Adam Heard the Voice of Sin
description: When Adam Heard the Voice of Sin in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the East (Paisley, in print by 1911).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: When A-dam heard the voice of sin And fell be-fore its power, The flowers of Par-a-dise were shorn Of beau-ty in that hour.

lines: When Adam heard the voice of sin
And fell before its power,
The flowers of Paradise were shorn
Of beauty in that hour.
And clouds obscured the heavenly light,
And e'en the stars were dim;
For O 'twas night, and only night,
Dark night 'twixt God and him.
"O whence that flashing sword that gleams?
And whence those angels there?"
Out from the garden of their bliss,
Was thrust the guilty pair.
Life is not theirs, the tree of Life
The Cherubim surround;
Death dogs our guilty parents' steps,
Curse blasts the fertile ground.
O dreary, dreary, dark and dread,
O misery of sin!
"God make another garden fair,
And take Thy wanderers in."
All praise to Christ our glorious Lord,
For sin and death are slain;
The gates of heaven are open wide,
And life is ours again.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the East (by 1911)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the East; set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
